pathway_does: Ligand binding dimerises the receptor and switches on RAS-MAPK and PI3K-AKT; both branches drive proliferation and survival.
role: Receptor tyrosine kinase at the cell surface — the ligand-binding member of the HER family.
drugged_neighbours: ERBB2; KRAS; PIK3CA; BRAF; MAP2K1; MTOR
note: Role and pathway from the UniProt Function section. The neighbours are targets on the same cascade that already carry approved drugs.

pathway_does: The same cascade EGFR runs — RAS-MAPK and PI3K-AKT — entered through a receptor pair rather than a ligand.
role: Receptor tyrosine kinase with no ligand of its own; it works as the preferred dimerisation partner of the other HER receptors, which is why amplification alone drives signalling.
note: Role and pathway from the UniProt Function section. The neighbours are targets on the same cascade that already carry approved drugs.

pathway_does: A GTPase switch downstream of receptor tyrosine kinases; in the GTP-bound state it turns on RAF-MEK-ERK.
role: Small GTPase, lipid-anchored on the cytoplasmic face of the membrane — which is why antibodies and ADCs cannot reach it.
drugged_neighbours: EGFR; ERBB2; BRAF; MAP2K1; PTPN11; SOS1
note: Role and pathway from the UniProt Function section. Neighbours are nodes of the same cascade with drugs in the clinic or on the market.

pathway_does: Engagement by PD-L1 recruits the phosphatase SHP-2 to the T-cell receptor complex and damps signalling, limiting the response.
role: Cell-surface inhibitory receptor induced on activated T cells.
note: Role and pathway from the UniProt Function section. Neighbours are other checkpoint receptors and ligands with approved or late-stage drugs.

pathway_does: Lowers the threshold at which the B-cell receptor fires by amplifying PI3K signalling.
role: B-cell surface co-receptor — expressed from the pro-B stage through to most B-cell malignancies.
note: Role from the UniProt Function section. Neighbours are the other B-cell surface antigens and BCR-pathway nodes that carry approved drugs.

pathway: BAFF / APRIL receptor signalling in plasma cells
pathway_does: BAFF and APRIL binding drives plasma-cell survival through NF-kB, which is the dependency myeloma inherits.
drugged_neighbours: restricted to plasma cells and plasmablasts.
column8: Role and pathway from the UniProt Function section. Neighbours are the other receptors and the shared ligand of the same axis.

pathway: BAFF receptor signalling into non-canonical NF-kB
pathway_does: BAFF binding stabilises NIK, which processes p100 to p52 — the arm of NF-kB that keeps mature B cells alive.
role: TNF-family receptor on mature B cells; the arm of the axis that is B-cell selective rather than plasma-cell selective.
note: Role and pathway from the UniProt Function section. Neighbours are the ligand it binds and the kinase it signals through.

pathway_does: The ligand side of the same axis: one cytokine, three receptors, and blocking it hits all three at once.
role: Secreted TNF-family cytokine; also exists as a membrane form.
note: Role and pathway from the UniProt Function section. Neighbours are its three receptors — the reason a ligand programme and a receptor programme are different products.

pathway: TL1A - DR3 signalling in mucosal immunity
pathway_does: Binding DR3 on T cells amplifies whatever response is already running, which is why the target is pursued in IBD rather than in infection.
note: Role and pathway from the UniProt Function section. Neighbours are its receptor and the cytokines targeted in the same disease.

pathway_does: Drives and maintains Th17 cells through JAK-STAT; the p40 subunit it pairs with is shared with IL-12, which is what separates a p19 antibody from a p40 one.
role: Cytokine subunit — the p19 chain of IL-23; it is only active paired with p40.
note: Role and pathway from the UniProt Function section. Neighbours are the shared subunit
column9: the downstream kinase and the effector cytokine — all with approved drugs.

pathway_does: Held at a low level by a degradation complex and stabilised when a receptor signals; it then processes p100 to p52.
role: Kinase — the committed step of the non-canonical arm
source_url: so only small molecules and degraders can reach it.
column9: Role and pathway from the UniProt Function section. Neighbours are the receptors that signal into it and the kinase downstream; none of them has an approved drug that works through this arm.

pathway: C-type lectin receptor signalling in myeloid cells
pathway_does: Assembles the CARD9-BCL10-MALT1 complex downstream of Dectin-1, turning fungal recognition into NF-kB activation.
role: Cytosolic adaptor — a scaffold rather than an enzyme
drugged_neighbours: which is what makes it hard to drug.
column8: Role and pathway from the UniProt Function section. Neighbours are the receptor above it and the enzymes below it; the enzymes are where the tractability is.

pathway_does: Dephosphorylates LCK and ZAP70 to damp the T-cell receptor, which is why the risk allele sits in several autoimmune diseases.
column9: Role and pathway from the UniProt Function section. Neighbours are its substrates and the phosphatase family member that has been drugged.

pathway: Inhibitory receptor signalling on myeloid cells
pathway_does: An ITIM-bearing receptor that recruits SHP-1 and SHP-2 and switches myeloid activation off — the myeloid counterpart of a checkpoint.
role: Cell-surface inhibitory receptor, expressed on monocytic AML.
note: Role and pathway from the UniProt Function section. Neighbours are the other myeloid checkpoints being pursued for the same reason.

pathway_does: Not a signalling cascade. Claudins seal the space between epithelial cells, and the 18.2 splice variant is confined to gastric mucosa — normally buried in the junction and exposed only when the tissue becomes malignant.
role: Four-pass membrane protein; the accessibility of the 18.2 isoform on tumour cells, not a pathway role, is the whole reason it is a target.
note: Role from the UniProt Function section. There is no downstream node to list here: the neighbours are other surface antigens on the same tumours, which is the honest analogue when a target is structural rather than a signalling node.
